name: Elara Voss

loved: {item}?! You remembered what I like. This is perfect.
Oh, {item}... I'm going to cry on the first page.
liked: Thank you. I'll keep it where I can see it while I work.
hated: Please keep that far away from the books.
Do you want the whole library to burn down?!

arrival: Oh! Hello. Sorry, I didn't expect anyone out here. I'm Elara. I've carried these books across half the country, and my arms may never forgive me.

arrival.say: I saw the smoke from your hearth and... well. A village with shelves enough for a library? May I settle here?

reply: Truly? Thank you, {player}. I promise to be a good neighbour. And a quiet one. Mostly.

choices.text: You can have the best shelf.
reply: The best shelf! I'm going to remember you said that.

arrival: I'll go and find my new front door. Thank you, {player}.
bouquet_accept: Is this... for me? Flowers? In a library?
*She hides her smile behind the bouquet.*
Yes, {player}. I would like that. Very much.
bouquet_reject: That's very sweet. But I think we should know each other a little better first.
pendant_accept: Is that a pendant? {player}... are you...
Yes. A thousand times yes. Give me three days to finish my speech, and a quiet dress.
pendant_reject: Oh! I'm not ready for that. Please, give me time.
wedding: *The whole village gathers at the hearth. Elara walks toward you with ink-stained fingers and a crown of wildflowers.*
I'm nervous. I've written this speech eleven times and thrown ten of them away.

wedding.say: I, Elara Voss, promise to keep your name on every title page of my life. Will you have me, {player}?

reply: Then it's settled. Partner. My favourite word.
Then it's settled. Partner. My favourite word.

greetings.say: It's my birthday and you're here. Maybe this will be a good year after all.
Rain on the roof is the best soundtrack for a library, don't you think?
Rain, a lantern, a book, and you. I couldn't have designed it better.
Oh, hello. Do you need help finding something?
Shh... well, you're allowed to talk. A little.
{player}! I saved you the seat by the window.
Looking for a book, or just good company?
You're becoming a regular, {player}. I rather like it.
Sundays are for rereading old favourites.
Good morning. I've already catalogued six shelves and I'm very pleased with myself.
The lantern hours are my favourite. Everything feels like the start of a story.
I catch myself listening for your footsteps. Is that strange?
Welcome home, {player}. I kept your tea warm.
I found a page of my novel in your coat pocket. You've been rereading it, haven't you?

script: {player}? Oh, you startled me. I was counting spines. It's a thing I do.

script.say: Tell me, since you're here: what do you reach for when you want to lose an afternoon?

reply: Dragons and ruined castles? Yes! I have a whole shelf. Don't tell anyone I read them twice.
A fellow cartographer of the mind. I'll set the good atlases aside for you.

choices.text: Honestly, I just like the quiet.
reply: ...That might be the nicest thing anyone has said about this room.

script: Come back any time. The quiet is free.
Have you seen a green book with a cracked spine? 'Tides of Ember'? I'd swear I shelved it, but it has simply... gone.

script.say: It isn't even valuable. It's the first book I ever borrowed, when I was small.

reply: *She lifts the cushion. The green book is right there.*
You found it! How did you know?
I'll never lose it again. Thank you, {player}.
Maybe. I'll ask around. Thank you for not laughing.
Just a book. Of course.

script: Rain this loud makes the shelves hum. Do you hear it?

script.say: I read aloud during storms. Would you mind sitting a while?

reply: *She reads by lantern light, and the rain forgets to be loud.*
Thank you for staying, {player}.
Funny! One moment... the dragon who was afraid of fire.
*You laugh in all the right places. She notices.*
Of course. Mind the puddles.

script: Before you say anything: nobody has read this. Not one page.
*She sets a thick stack of pages on the desk, tied with blue thread.*

script.say: It's a novel. About a lighthouse keeper who writes letters to the sea. Please be honest.

reply: You haven't read a word yet! ...But thank you.

choices.text: Read me your favourite page first.
reply: *Her voice shakes on the first line and steadies by the last.*
That's the first time I've said it out loud. Thank you.

choices.text: Who would publish letters to the sea?
reply: Right. Practical. Of course. Forget I asked.

script: I'll keep writing. Even if only you read it.
*Evening. The library is dark except for one lantern. Elara waits by the door.*
{player}. I wanted to show you something. Come with me?
*She leads you up a narrow stair to the roof. The sky is thick with stars.*

script.say: I've spent my whole life inside other people's stories. But you feel like the first chapter that's mine.

reply: *She smiles, and for once she doesn't look away.*
I'd like that more than anything.

choices.text: Take your time. I'm not going anywhere.
reply: That might be the most romantic sentence I've ever heard.

script: {player}, come here. I finished it. The book.
*She opens the cover. The dedication reads: 'For the one who stayed.'*

script.say: I couldn't have written the ending without you.

choices.text: Read it to me. Start to finish.
reply: All night, if you like.
*She hugs you, and the pages rustle between you like applause.*

script: Home is wherever you are, {player}. And I'm going to keep it well stocked with books.
